topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: Under the 2025 Code of Georgia, which insurer is a domestic insurer?

options.A: An insurer formed under the laws of another U.S. state
options.B: An insurer formed under the laws of Georgia
options.C: An insurer formed under the laws of a country other than the United States
options.D: Any insurer holding a certificate of authority, wherever it was formed

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-3-1(4) (2025 Code of Georgia, Justia compilation) defines a domestic insurer as an insurer formed under the laws of Georgia. A foreign insurer is formed under the laws of another state or government of the United States (§ 33-3-1(5)). An alien insurer is formed under the laws of a country other than the United States (§ 33-3-1(2)). Formation, not the license alone, is what these three labels use.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: An insurer organized in Alabama that is licensed to do business in Georgia is classified in O.C.G.A. § 33-3-1 as:

options.A: A domestic insurer
options.B: An alien insurer
options.C: A foreign insurer
options.D: A surplus lines broker

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-3-1(5) defines a foreign insurer as one formed under the laws of another state or government of the United States. Alabama is another U.S. state, so the insurer is foreign to Georgia. Alien status is reserved for formation under the laws of a country other than the United States.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: An insurer formed under the laws of Canada is, for O.C.G.A. § 33-3-1, an:

options.A: Alien insurer
options.B: Domestic insurer
options.C: Foreign insurer
options.D: Unauthorized domestic insurer

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-3-1(2) defines an alien insurer as an insurer formed under the laws of a country other than the United States. Foreign, in the same section, means formed under the laws of another U.S. state or government of the United States.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: Which act does O.C.G.A. § 33-6-4(b)(2) treat as an unfair method of competition or a deceptive practice?

options.A: A dividend estimate on company forms that clearly says, in type as large as the figures, that the figures are estimates based on past company experience
options.B: A misrepresentation made to a policyholder to induce the policyholder to lapse, forfeit, or surrender insurance
options.C: Paying commissions to a duly licensed agent
options.D: Returning dividends to participating policyholders

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-6-4(b)(2) (2025 Code) includes making a misrepresentation to a policyholder for the purpose of inducing or tending to induce lapse, forfeiture, or surrender. The same paragraph says a dividend estimate prepared on company forms, with the estimate nature shown in type equal in size to the figures and based on past company experience, is not misrepresentation under that paragraph. Paying commissions to licensed agents and returning dividends to participating policyholders are listed among practices that are not rebates or discrimination under § 33-6-4(b)(8)(C).

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: Publishing a statement that is false or maliciously critical of an insurer's financial condition, calculated to injure a person in the insurance business, is addressed in Georgia law as:

options.A: An allowed conservation effort
options.B: An unfair method of competition or deceptive practice under O.C.G.A. § 33-6-4(b)(3)
options.C: A required replacement notice
options.D: A fiduciary accounting under O.C.G.A. § 33-23-35

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-6-4(b)(3) deems it an unfair method of competition or a deceptive practice to make, publish, disseminate, or circulate an oral or written statement that is false or maliciously critical of, or substantially misrepresents, the financial condition of an insurer and is calculated to injure a person engaged in the insurance business. This is the statute's defamation-style prohibition. It is not the life-replacement notice in Rule 120-2-24 and it is not the premium-fiduciary rule.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: O.C.G.A. § 33-6-4(b)(4) prohibits:

options.A: Any difference in premium between two different classes of risk
options.B: An agreement or concerted boycott, coercion, or intimidation that results or tends to result in unreasonable restraint of, or a monopoly in, the insurance business
options.C: Filing a true financial statement with the Commissioner
options.D: A spouse buying insurance on the other spouse

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-6-4(b)(4) covers entering an agreement to commit, or by concerted action committing, any act of boycott, coercion, or intimidation resulting in or tending to result in unreasonable restraint of or a monopoly in the business of insurance. Different premiums for different risk classes are not what this paragraph forbids. Consent between spouses is a separate rule in § 33-24-6.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: For life insurance or a life annuity, O.C.G.A. § 33-6-4(b)(8)(A)(i) treats which comparison as unfair discrimination?

options.A: Different rates for people who are not of the same class
options.B: Unfair discrimination in rates, dividends, or other terms between individuals of the same class, same policy amount, and equal expectation of life
options.C: A lower rate for bona fide employees of the insurer than for other persons in the same class
options.D: A payroll-deduction plan priced to reflect the insurer's savings from that plan

explanation: Section 33-6-4(b)(8)(A)(i) prohibits unfair discrimination between individuals of the same class, same policy amount, and equal expectation of life in rates, dividends or other benefits, or other terms of a life or life-annuity contract. Subparagraph (C) says the section's discrimination and rebate rules do not include issuing life or accident-and-sickness policies to bona fide employees of the insurer at a lower rate than other persons in the same class, or issuing policies on a salary-saving or payroll-deduction plan at a reduced rate commensurate with the savings.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: Unfair discrimination in accident or sickness premiums, under O.C.G.A. § 33-6-4(b)(8)(A)(ii), is discrimination between individuals who are:

options.A: Of the same class and of essentially the same hazard
options.B: In different occupations with different hazards
options.C: Buying property insurance in different fire districts
options.D: Residents of different countries

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-6-4(b)(8)(A)(ii) addresses unfair discrimination between individuals of the same class and of essentially the same hazard in premium, policy fees, or rates for accident or sickness insurance, in the benefits, or in any terms of the contract. The residential-property fire-district rule is a different subparagraph and is not the accident-and-sickness standard.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 33-6-4(b)(8)(A)(iv)(I), an insurer refuses to continue a policy because of the applicant's race. That refusal is:

options.A: Allowed if the rate manual was filed
options.B: An unfair and deceptive act or practice in connection with any kind of insurance
options.C: A permitted employee-rate difference
options.D: Outside the unfair-trade statute because it is not a life case

explanation: The 2025 text of O.C.G.A. § 33-6-4(b)(8)(A)(iv)(I) says unfair discrimination prohibited there includes discrimination based on race, color, and national or ethnic origin. It also says that, in connection with any kind of insurance, it is an unfair and deceptive act or practice to refuse to insure or to continue to insure, to limit coverage, or to charge a different rate for the same coverage because of race, color, or national or ethnic origin.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: An agent offers a prospect a rebate of premium that is not specified in the policy and is not part of a rate filing approved by the Commissioner. Under O.C.G.A. § 33-6-4(b)(8)(B), this is:

options.A: Required on every replacement
options.B: An unfair method of competition or a deceptive practice
options.C: Allowed up to $100 only if it is contingent on the sale
options.D: A fiduciary remittance under § 33-23-35

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-6-4(b)(8)(B) includes paying, allowing, or offering a rebate of premium, or any valuable consideration not specified in the contract, as an inducement, except in accordance with an applicable rate filing, rating plan, or rating system filed with and approved by the Commissioner. It also covers accepting such a rebate. The $100 promotional exception in § 33-6-4(b)(8)(C)(x) is the opposite of a sale contingency: the item must not be contingent on sale or renewal.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: A Georgia producer gives current customers store gift cards during the year. O.C.G.A. § 33-6-4(b)(8)(C)(x) says this promotional program is not a rebate or discrimination when the items:

options.A: Are given only after the customer buys or renews a policy
options.B: Exceed $100 in aggregate value per customer in that calendar year
options.C: Do not exceed $100 in aggregate value per customer in any one calendar year and are not contingent on the sale or renewal of a policy
options.D: Are shares of the insurer's stock

explanation: Section 33-6-4(b)(8)(C)(x) excludes from the discrimination and rebate definitions advertising or promotional programs in which prizes, goods, store gift cards, gift certificates, sporting-event tickets, or merchandise, not exceeding $100.00 in value per customer in the aggregate in any one calendar year, are given to current or prospective customers, provided the item is not contingent on the sale or renewal of a policy. Stock or other securities offered as an inducement are treated in the rebate paragraph, not in this exception.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: An agent pays for refreshments at a group seminar for prospective clients. Under O.C.G.A. § 33-6-4(b)(8)(C)(viii), that payment is not treated as a rebate or discrimination if:

options.A: Applications are accepted at the seminar
options.B: No insurance or annuity applications or contracts are offered or accepted at the presentation or seminar
options.C: Each guest receives a policy at the door
options.D: The refreshments are offered only to people who bind coverage that day

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-6-4(b)(8)(C)(viii) lists paying for food or refreshments by an insurer or an agent, broker, or employee for current or prospective clients during group sales presentations and group seminars, provided that no insurance or annuity applications or contracts are offered or accepted at those presentations or seminars. Accepting applications at the event removes this stated exception.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: A Georgia agent deposits a customer's premium into the agent's personal checking account and spends part of it on rent before sending the balance to the insurer. O.C.G.A. § 33-23-35(b) says premium funds must be:

options.A: Treated as a personal loan the agent may use if it is repaid within the month
options.B: Accounted for in a fiduciary capacity, not commingled with personal funds, and promptly paid to the person entitled to them
options.C: Kept only if the agent maintains a separate bank for every insurer, with no exception
options.D: Reported on the license renewal and otherwise unrestricted

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-23-35(b), as published in the 2025 Code of Georgia (Justia and Georgia Commons agree on this text), says funds representing premiums received, or return premiums due the insured, by an agent or subagent shall be accounted for in the licensee's fiduciary capacity, shall not be commingled with personal funds, and shall be promptly accounted for and paid to the insurer, insured, or agent entitled to them. The same subsection says a separate bank deposit for each principal is not required if the funds of each principal are reasonably ascertainable from the books. That bookkeeping option does not allow spending the premium as personal money.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: Must a Georgia agent keep a separate bank account for every insurer whose premium the agent holds?

options.A: Yes. Section 33-23-35 requires one deposit account per principal with no exception
options.B: No. A separate deposit for each principal is not required if the funds of each principal are reasonably ascertainable from the agent's books and records
options.C: Yes, but only for alien insurers
options.D: No, because premium may be commingled with personal funds if the agent is licensed

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-23-35(b) states that nothing in that Code section requires an agent or subagent to maintain a separate bank deposit for the funds of each principal if those funds are reasonably ascertainable from the books of account and records. The fiduciary duty and the ban on commingling with personal funds still apply.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: Under the 2025 text of O.C.G.A. § 33-23-35(c), a willful violation is a felony when the amounts involved:

options.A: Exceed $100
options.B: Exceed $500, which was the figure before the 2019 amendment
options.C: Exceed $1,000
options.D: Are any positive amount

explanation: The 2025 Code of Georgia text of § 33-23-35(c) on Justia says any willful violation is a misdemeanor unless the amounts involved exceed $1,000.00, in which case it is a felony. Justia's history note says a 2019 amendment, effective July 1, 2019, substituted $1,000.00 for $500.00. Older reprints that still say $500 are not the 2025 text used here. Any violation is also grounds for Commissioner action, including probation, suspension, or revocation.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: O.C.G.A. § 33-23-35(a) requires an agent or other representative who effectuates an insurance contract to:

options.A: Report the premium to the insurer or its agent, and show that amount in the contract
options.B: Keep the premium amount off the contract so the customer sees only the modal quote
options.C: Report the premium only at license renewal
options.D: Send the premium to the Georgia Life and Health Insurance Guaranty Association

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-23-35(a) says an agent, limited subagent, or any other representative of an insurer, or of any other person in the effectuation of an insurance contract, shall report to the insurer or its agent the premium for the contract, and the amount shall be shown in the contract. A willful violation of that subsection is a misdemeanor.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: The Pearson VUE Georgia Candidate Handbook #121100 (October 2026) states the passing rule as:

options.A: 65% after pretest questions are removed by the candidate
options.B: 70% of questions answered correctly
options.C: A scaled score of 80 that the candidate computes from a formula in the handbook
options.D: 50% on the state section and 70% on the national section, scored separately

explanation: Handbook #121100, October 2026, in the score explanation, says the score is the percentage of questions answered correctly and: "You need to answer 70% of questions correctly in order to pass the examination." The same handbook says the passing score was set by the Georgia Insurance Department and that equating is used across forms. It does not give candidates a split national/state cut score. Pretest items, described later in the handbook, do not affect the score, but they are not identified and the candidate does not remove them. This practice simulator grades every item it shows.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: On the official Pearson VUE Georgia agent exams, pretest questions:

options.A: Are marked "pretest" and may be skipped without affecting the result
options.B: Are mixed with scored questions, are not identified, and do not affect the score
options.C: Are the only questions that count toward the 70%
options.D: Are omitted from Life and from Accident and Sickness, and used only on the combo exam

explanation: Candidate Handbook #121100 (October 2026) says many examinations contain pretest questions used to build future exams. Responses do not affect the score. Pretest questions are mixed with scored questions and are not identified. Content outline #121102 (effective October 22, 2024; PDF header #121102 rev09/2026) lists 10 pretest questions on the Life outline, 10 on the Accident and Sickness outline, and 10 on the Life, Accident and Sickness outline. This hub's practice sim does not hide unscored items.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: In the October 2026 handbook fee table, which pairing of exam code, name, and time is correct?

options.A: 12-GA-01 Life Agent, 2 hours; 12-GA-02 Accident/Sickness Agent, 2 hours; 12-GA-05 Life/Accident/Sickness Agent combo, 2.5 hours. Each listed fee is $67
options.B: 12-GA-05 is Life only and is 2 hours
options.C: 12-GA-01 is the combo exam and is 4 hours
options.D: The combo exam is 90 minutes and costs $100

explanation: The Available Examinations and Fees table in Handbook #121100 (October 2026) lists 12-GA-01 Life Agent at 2 hours, 12-GA-02 Accident/Sickness Agent at 2 hours, and 12-GA-05 Life/Accident/Sickness Agent COMBO at 2.5 hours. The exam fee column for those rows is $67. Those three rows are also marked as available in Spanish. The $100 figure in a different table is the agent license fee, not the exam fee.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: A candidate fails the Georgia Life Agent exam for the second time. The October 2026 handbook's retake policy says the candidate:

options.A: May not take that exam again
options.B: Must wait 60 days after the second attempt
options.C: Can schedule the new exam within one day, but must wait 14 days to retest after attempts one and two
options.D: Must wait 14 days only after the fifth attempt

explanation: Handbook #121100 states: a candidate who fails can schedule the new exam within one day but must wait fourteen (14) days to retest after exam attempts one and two. A candidate must wait 60 days after the third attempt and any subsequent attempts. There is no limit on the number of attempts. A separate sentence says candidates must wait twenty-four (24) hours before scheduling a reexamination. This practice item uses the retake-policy sentence for attempts one and two.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: After a candidate passes the Georgia examination, the October 2026 handbook says the candidate should apply for the license:

options.A: By mailing a paper form only to Pearson VUE in Bloomington
options.B: Online at www.sircon.com/georgia
options.C: By calling Pearson and requesting that the score be given over the telephone
options.D: Only after a 90-day waiting period that applies to every first-time applicant

explanation: Handbook #121100 says: after passing the examination, apply for the license online at www.sircon.com/georgia, and points readers to https://oci.ga.gov for more licensing information. It also says examination results will not be given by phone. The 90-day period in the handbook is about applying for a Georgia resident license after a former resident license becomes inactive, for an exemption from prelicensing, the exam, and fingerprints. It is not a wait imposed on every passer.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: How long does the October 2026 handbook say a Georgia prelicensing course remains valid?

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 90 days
options.C: One year, and the Pearson exam must be passed within that year of completing the course
options.D: Two years, matching the license term

explanation: Handbook #121100 states that prelicensing training courses are valid for one (1) year and that applicants must pass the Pearson licensure examination within one year of completing the prelicensing training. If they do not, they must retrain. The two-year period described elsewhere is the agent license term, not the course validity.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: For a new Georgia resident license applicant, the October 2026 handbook describes fingerprinting and the citizenship affidavit as:

options.A: Optional exhibits that Pearson collects at the test center
options.B: Fingerprints through Identogo after the Sircon application, and a notarized Citizenship Affidavit (GID-276-EN) uploaded with the application
options.C: A requirement that applies only to nonresident licenses
options.D: A substitute for the examination

explanation: Handbook #121100 says new resident applicants (with stated exceptions for active licensees and certain reinstatements) submit electronic fingerprints, and that the applicant applies at www.sircon.com/georgia before registering to fingerprint at ga.state.identogo.com/ata. It also says new license applicants submit a notarized Citizenship Affidavit Form (GID-276-EN) on U.S. citizenship or lawful presence, uploaded with the application at the NIPR warehouse or Sircon portal. The handbook's fingerprint procedure link is on oci.georgia.gov. These steps are not a waiver of the exam.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: The October 2026 handbook describes the Georgia agent license term as:

options.A: A one-year license that always expires on December 31
options.B: A two-year license that expires on the last day of the licensee's birth month, with a first term that can run about 18 to 29 months depending on birth month
options.C: A six-month license that converts automatically into a permanent license
options.D: A license that expires 90 days after the exam

explanation: Handbook #121100 says the Georgia Insurance Department issues a two-year agent license that expires on the last day of the licensee's birth month, so a new license can have an initial term ranging between 18 and 29 months depending on birth month. A temporary license is a different license: the handbook says the initial temporary license is issued for six months and that temporary licenses do not transfer or convert to a resident agent license.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: After the agent license is issued, the October 2026 handbook says the licensee must:

options.A: Obtain a certificate of authority from each insurer the licensee will represent
options.B: Stop selling until the next birth month
options.C: Post a $5,000 counselor bond before any appointment
options.D: Retake the exam every two years

explanation: Handbook #121100 says: upon issuance of the agent license, the licensee must obtain a certificate of authority from each insurer that they will represent. The $5,000 bond in the handbook table is listed for the Life and Accident & Sickness Counselor row (form GID-112), not as the condition of an agent appointment. The handbook does not say the exam is retaken every license term.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: Which statement matches the October 2026 handbook's description of a temporary insurance agent license?

options.A: A person may hold a new temporary license as often as the person changes insurers, and it converts to a resident agent license
options.B: It is limited to one temporary license per lifetime, the initial license is six months, a sponsoring insurer and supervising agent are required, and it does not convert to a resident agent license
options.C: It requires the full prelicensing course and the Pearson exam
options.D: It is available only to nonresidents

explanation: Handbook #121100 says a temporary insurance agent sells, solicits, or negotiates through one specific insurer; the insurer sponsors the person; a supervising agent must be licensed and appointed with that insurer; a licensee is limited to one temporary license per lifetime; the initial license is issued for six months; and temporary licenses do not transfer or convert to a resident agent license. The exam table lists the temporary agent as "(No exam)."

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: A producer moving a resident license to Georgia lets the old resident license become inactive. The October 2026 handbook says that, to be eligible for exemption from Georgia prelicensing, the exam, and fingerprints, the producer has:

options.A: 90 days to apply for the Georgia resident license
options.B: One year, the same period as prelicensing-course validity
options.C: 14 days, the same period as an exam retake
options.D: No time limit

explanation: Handbook #121100 says that to transfer a resident license the person requests a letter of clearance from the former state, and that once the license is inactive the person has ninety (90) days to apply for the Georgia resident license to be eligible to be exempted from prelicensing courses, exams, and fingerprinting. That 90-day statement is separate from the one-year validity of a prelicensing course and from the exam retake waits.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: The October 2026 handbook's instruction on guessing is:

options.A: Leave doubtful items blank because wrong answers subtract points
options.B: There is no penalty for an incorrect answer, and it is better to answer than to leave an item blank
options.C: Only the state-law items may be guessed
options.D: Pretest items should be left blank so they are not scored

explanation: Handbook #121100 says scores are based on the number of questions answered correctly, there is no penalty for incorrect answers, and it is better to provide an answer than not to answer. Pretest items are not identified, so a candidate cannot single them out to leave blank.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: The October 2026 handbook fee table shows the agent license charge, separate from the $67 exam fee, as:

options.A: License $100 and processing fee $20
options.B: License $67 and no processing fee
options.C: License $600, the nonresident surplus lines figure
options.D: License $50, which is the temporary-agent license row

explanation: In the resident agent rows of the handbook table, including Life, Accident & Sickness, and Life and Accident & Sickness, the fee column reads License: $100 and Processing Fee: $20. The $67 amount is the exam fee in the examinations table. The $50 license amount is on the temporary-agent row. The $600 amount is on the nonresident surplus lines broker row. Those are handbook table figures, not figures from a Code section read for this project.

topic: Georgia laws common to life and accident and sickness
question: Which of these Georgia agent exams does the October 2026 handbook mark as available in Spanish?

options.A: None of the life or accident exams
options.B: Life Agent, Accident/Sickness Agent, and the Life/Accident/Sickness combo
options.C: Only the surplus lines broker exam
options.D: Only the counselor exams

explanation: The handbook fee table puts an asterisk on 12-GA-01, 12-GA-02, and 12-GA-05, and the footnote says "Exam available in Spanish." The asterisk also appears on some other exams, including property, casualty, and the property-casualty combo. It is not limited to surplus lines or counselor exams, and it is not absent from the life and accident rows.

topic: Georgia rules for life insurance only
question: Georgia Rule 120-2-24 states that its purpose is to:

options.A: Set Medicare supplement open-enrollment dates
options.B: Protect life insurance policyholders by setting minimum standards for replacement or proposed replacement of existing life insurance
options.C: Require a separate bank account for every insurer
options.D: Ban all replacements of life insurance

explanation: Rule 120-2-24-.02, on the Georgia Secretary of State rules site, says the regulation protects the interests of life insurance policyholders by establishing minimum standards of conduct for the replacement or proposed replacement of existing life insurance. It does not ban replacement. Premium bank accounts are § 33-23-35. Medicare supplement rules are a different chapter.

topic: Georgia rules for life insurance only
question: Under Rule 120-2-24-.03(12), a replacement includes a transaction in which new life insurance or an annuity will be purchased and, as a result, existing life insurance will be:

options.A: Left completely unchanged
options.B: Lapsed, forfeited, surrendered, or otherwise terminated, or reduced in value by a nonforfeiture benefit or a policy loan, or reduced in benefits or term, or reissued with a reduction in cash value
options.C: Converted from term to permanent with no reduction and no lapse
options.D: Continued by a family member who was already the beneficiary

explanation: Rule 120-2-24-.03(12) defines replacement as a transaction in which new life insurance or an annuity has been or is to be purchased, and the proposing agent, counselor, or insurer knows or should know that existing life insurance has been or is to be lapsed, forfeited, surrendered, or otherwise terminated; changed to reduced paid-up or extended term or otherwise reduced in value by nonforfeiture benefits, policy loans, or other policy values; amended to reduce benefits or the term; or reissued with any reduction in cash value.

topic: Georgia rules for life insurance only
question: Rule 120-2-24-.04 says the replacement regulation does not apply, unless specifically included, to which of these?

options.A: Replacement of an individual whole life policy with a new individual whole life policy
options.B: Replacement of annuity contracts, credit life insurance, and group life insurance
options.C: Every annuity funded with a life-policy surrender
options.D: Any policy still inside the unconditional refund period

explanation: Rule 120-2-24-.04 lists exemptions that include replacement of annuity contracts, credit life insurance, and group life insurance, plus certain life insurance in pension or similar plans when the stated conditions are met. Existing life insurance is defined to include coverage under a binding or conditional receipt or within the unconditional refund period, so being inside that period does not by itself create the exemption. Replacing one individual whole life policy with another is the kind of transaction the duties address when the definition is met.

topic: Georgia rules for life insurance only
question: When a replacement is involved, Rule 120-2-24-.05 requires the agent to present the Replacement Notice:

options.A: Within 30 days after delivery, signed only by the insurer
options.B: Not later than at the time of taking the application, signed by the applicant and the agent, and left with the applicant
options.C: Only if the applicant asks for it after the free-look period
options.D: To the Georgia Life and Health Insurance Guaranty Association instead of the applicant

explanation: Rule 120-2-24-.05(2)(a) says the agent shall present to the applicant, not later than at the time of taking the application, a Replacement Notice as described in Exhibit A or another substantially similar form approved by the Commissioner. The notice shall be signed by both the applicant and the agent and left with the applicant.

topic: Georgia rules for life insurance only
question: Rule 120-2-24-.05 requires the list of existing life insurance to be replaced to identify that insurance by:

options.A: Premium only
options.B: Name of insurer, insured, and policy number, or another identifier such as an application or receipt number if no policy number exists
options.C: The agent's national producer number only
options.D: The beneficiary's Social Security number

explanation: Rule 120-2-24-.05(2)(b) says the agent obtains, with or as part of each application, a list of all existing life insurance to be replaced, identified by name of insurer, insured, and policy number. If the existing insurer has not assigned a policy number, an alternative such as an application or receipt number is listed.

topic: Georgia rules for life insurance only
question: If an agent uses written advertisements in the sales presentation for a replacement, Rule 120-2-24-.05 says the agent must:

options.A: Destroy them after the application is signed
options.B: Leave with the applicant the original or a copy of all written or printed advertisements used in the presentation
options.C: File them only with the existing insurer and not leave a copy
options.D: Read them aloud and keep the only copy

explanation: Rule 120-2-24-.05(2)(c) requires the agent to leave with the applicant the original or a copy of all written or printed advertisements used in the presentation. A separate paragraph requires an agent who uses written advertisements in a conservation to leave the original or a copy of those conservation advertisements as well.

topic: Georgia rules for life insurance only
question: Under Rule 120-2-24-.07, a replacing insurer that uses agents mails the Replacement Notice and the written notice of the replacement to the existing insurer:

options.A: Within three working days of the date the application is received in the replacing insurer's home or regional office, or the date the proposed policy is issued, whichever is sooner
options.B: Within ten working days after the free look ends
options.C: Only if the applicant checks that a policy summary is wanted
options.D: Within one year, when the record-retention period ends

explanation: Rule 120-2-24-.07(2)(b) says the Replacement Notice and written communication shall be mailed within three (3) working days of the date the application is received in the replacing insurer's home or regional office, or the date the proposed policy is issued, whichever is sooner. The ten-working-day period in Rule 120-2-24-.06(5) is the existing insurer's time to furnish a policy summary if indicated or requested. The three-year period is a record-keeping period, not the mailing deadline.

topic: Georgia rules for life insurance only
question: An existing insurer receives a Replacement Notice and a request for a policy summary. Rule 120-2-24-.06(5) says the insurer furnishes the policy summary to the present policyholder:

options.A: Within ten working days after receipt
options.B: Within three working days, which is the replacing insurer's mailing rule
options.C: Only at the next triennial examination
options.D: Never, because conservation is prohibited

explanation: Rule 120-2-24-.06(5) says an insurer that receives a Replacement Notice and written communication that its existing insurance may be replaced shall, within ten (10) working days after receipt, furnish a policy summary statement to the present policyholder if so indicated or requested. Conservation is defined in the rule and is not banned. The three-working-day clock is the replacing insurer's mailing duty in Rule 120-2-24-.07.

topic: Georgia rules for life insurance only
question: Rule 120-2-24-.06 requires replacing insurers to keep the Replacement Notice, required written communications, the applicant's statement, and a replacement register for:

options.A: Thirty days
options.B: At least three years, or until the conclusion of the next regular examination by the insurance department of the insurer's state of domicile, whichever is later
options.C: Until the free look ends
options.D: One year, matching prelicensing-course validity

explanation: Rule 120-2-24-.06(3) requires those copies to be maintained in the home office for at least three years or until the conclusion of the next succeeding regular examination by the insurance department of the insurer's state of domicile, whichever is later. The register is cross-indexed by replacing agent and existing insurer.

topic: Georgia rules for life insurance only
question: The Replacement Notice required by Rule 120-2-24, Exhibit A, tells the applicant that after receiving an individual life policy the applicant has:

options.A: Ten days to examine it and return it to the insurer's home or branch office, or to the agent, for a full refund of premium
options.B: Thirty days, and only a partial refund
options.C: Three working days, the same period as the insurer's mailing duty
options.D: No return right if a replacement notice was signed

explanation: Exhibit A to Rule 120-2-24, which is the Replacement Notice text on the Secretary of State rules page, says the applicant has ten (10) days following receipt of any individual life insurance policy to examine it and, if not satisfied for any reason, to return it to the insurer at its home or branch office or to the agent through whom it was purchased, for a full refund of premium. Signing a replacement notice does not remove that statement from the required notice.

topic: Georgia rules for life insurance only
question: O.C.G.A. § 33-24-3(a) defines an insurable interest in personal insurance as:

options.A: Any curiosity about a neighbor's health
options.B: A reasonable expectation of pecuniary advantage through the continued life, health, or bodily safety of another and a consequent loss from that person's death or disability, or a substantial interest from love and affection for individuals closely related by blood or by law
options.C: An interest that must still exist on the day of the claim
options.D: An interest that only the beneficiary, never the insured, may have

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-24-3(a) (2025 Code, Justia) uses that pecuniary-advantage test and the love-and-affection test for individuals closely related by blood or by law. Subsection (h) says the interest must exist when the contract of personal insurance becomes effective but need not exist when the loss occurs. Subsection (b) says an individual has an unlimited insurable interest in the individual's own life, health, and bodily safety and may name anyone as beneficiary, whether or not that beneficiary has an insurable interest. The Pearson outline's cross-reference "33-24-6" for insurable interest does not match this section title: the 2025 code places insurable interest in § 33-24-3 and consent of the insured in § 33-24-6.

topic: Georgia rules for life insurance only
question: A person buys a policy on the person's own life and names a friend who has no financial interest as beneficiary. O.C.G.A. § 33-24-3(b) says:

options.A: The designation is unlawful because every beneficiary must have an insurable interest
options.B: The person has an unlimited insurable interest in the person's own life and may have the policy payable to whomever the person pleases
options.C: The policy is valid only if the friend is a spouse
options.D: The interest must be rechecked at death

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-24-3(b) states that an individual has an unlimited insurable interest in the individual's own life, health, and bodily safety and may lawfully take out a policy on that life and have it payable to whomsoever the individual pleases, regardless of whether the beneficiary has an insurable interest. Section 33-24-3(h) says the insurable interest must exist when the contract becomes effective and need not exist when the loss occurs.

topic: Georgia rules for life insurance only
question: Someone who has no insurable interest procures a life policy on another person, payable to the procurer. Under O.C.G.A. § 33-24-3(i):

options.A: The contract is valid if the insured later consents at the claim
options.B: The contract is void, the insurer is not liable on it, and the insurer must repay the premiums without interest to the person who paid them
options.C: The insurer pays the death benefit and keeps the premiums
options.D: The contract is valid because insurable interest is required only at the time of loss

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-24-3(i) says a personal insurance contract procured or caused to be procured upon another individual is void unless the benefits are payable to the insured, the insured's personal representative, or a person who had an insurable interest when the contract was made. On a void contract the insurer is not liable on the contract but is liable to repay, without interest, the premiums to the persons who paid them. Subsection (h) requires the interest at inception, not at the loss.

topic: Georgia rules for life insurance only
question: O.C.G.A. § 33-24-6(a) generally forbids making an individual life or accident-and-sickness contract unless, at the time, the insured applies or consents in writing. Which exception is in that subsection?

options.A: Any friend may insure any other friend with no consent and no insurable interest
options.B: A spouse may effectuate insurance upon the other spouse
options.C: Group life is the only contract that ever requires consent
options.D: Consent is never required for corporate-owned life insurance on one employee

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-24-6(a) (2025 Code, Justia) says no life or accident and sickness contract upon an individual, except group life or group or blanket accident and sickness, shall be made unless the insured, being of competent legal capacity, applies or consents in writing, with listed exceptions. Exception (1) is that a spouse may effectuate insurance upon the other spouse. The section also addresses corporate-owned coverage and, in a later paragraph of the same section, requires written consent before issuance for life policies issued under the corporate paragraphs (4) and (5), including an acknowledgment that coverage may continue after employment ends. A friend with no insurable interest is not an exception.

topic: Georgia rules for accident and sickness only
question: O.C.G.A. § 33-43-1(6) defines a Medicare supplement policy as a policy that is:

options.A: Any major-medical plan sold to a person under 65
options.B: Advertised, marketed, or designed primarily as a supplement to Medicare reimbursements for hospital, medical, or surgical expenses of persons eligible for Medicare, other than the federal contract and demonstration-project policies the subsection excludes
options.C: Workers' compensation coverage
options.D: A long-term care policy advertised only as nursing-home insurance

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-43-1(6) (2025 Code, Justia) defines a Medicare supplement policy as a group or individual accident-and-sickness policy, or a subscriber contract of a hospital or medical service association or HMO, other than a policy issued under a contract under Section 1876 of the Social Security Act or a specified demonstration project, which is advertised, marketed, or designed primarily as a supplement to reimbursements under Medicare for the hospital, medical, or surgical expenses of persons eligible for Medicare. Long-term care is a different chapter.

topic: Georgia rules for accident and sickness only
question: For Medicare supplement creditable coverage in O.C.G.A. § 33-43-1(3.1), a continuous period of creditable coverage is a period during which breaks in coverage were:

options.A: No greater than 63 days
options.B: No greater than 30 days
options.C: No greater than one year
options.D: Unlimited

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-43-1(3.1) defines a continuous period of creditable coverage as the period during which an individual was covered by creditable coverage if during that period the individual had no breaks in coverage greater than 63 days.

topic: Georgia rules for accident and sickness only
question: Which coverage does O.C.G.A. § 33-43-1(3.2)(B) say is not creditable coverage for the Medicare supplement chapter?

options.A: A group health plan
options.B: Part A or Part B of Medicare
options.C: Workers' compensation or similar insurance
options.D: Medicaid, other than coverage consisting solely of benefits under Section 1928

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-43-1(3.2)(A) lists creditable coverage that includes a group health plan, health insurance coverage, Medicare Part A or Part B, and Medicaid other than coverage consisting solely of Section 1928 benefits. Subsection (3.2)(B) says creditable coverage shall not include workers' compensation or similar insurance, along with other listed coverages such as accident-only or disability-income coverage, liability insurance, and credit-only insurance.

topic: Georgia rules for accident and sickness only
question: Limited-scope dental or vision benefits are excluded from creditable coverage under O.C.G.A. § 33-43-1(3.2)(C) when they are:

options.A: An integral part of a health plan and not a separate policy
options.B: Provided under a separate policy, certificate, or contract, or are otherwise not an integral part of the plan
options.C: Medicare Part A
options.D: A group health plan's hospital benefit

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-43-1(3.2)(C) says creditable coverage shall not include limited-scope dental or vision benefits, long-term care or similar care, or other similar limited benefits specified in federal regulation as of July 1, 2000, if they are provided under a separate policy, certificate, or contract of insurance or are otherwise not an integral part of the plan.

topic: Georgia rules for accident and sickness only
question: In the Medicare supplement chapter, O.C.G.A. § 33-43-1(4) uses "issuer" to include:

options.A: Only stock life insurers domiciled in Georgia
options.B: Insurance companies, fraternal benefit societies, health care service plans, HMOs, and any other entity delivering or issuing Medicare supplement policies or certificates in this state
options.C: Only insurance agencies, not insurers
options.D: Only the federal Medicare program

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-43-1(4) says issuer includes insurance companies, fraternal benefit societies, health care service plans, health maintenance organizations, and any other entity delivering or issuing for delivery in this state Medicare supplement policies or certificates. The term is not limited to Georgia-domiciled stock life insurers and is not the Medicare program itself.

topic: Georgia rules for accident and sickness only
question: O.C.G.A. § 33-42-1 provides that Chapter 42:

options.A: May be known and cited as the Long-term Care Insurance Act
options.B: Is the Medicare supplement chapter
options.C: Repeals all other accident-and-sickness laws
options.D: Applies only to policies sold before 1988

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-42-1 (2025 Code, Justia) says this chapter may be known and cited as the Long-term Care Insurance Act. Medicare supplement insurance is Chapter 43. Section 33-42-3 says the chapter applies to long-term care insurance policies issued, delivered, or issued for delivery in this state, and a 2019 amendment deleted a former "on or after July 1, 1988" limitation from the first sentence.

topic: Georgia rules for accident and sickness only
question: O.C.G.A. § 33-42-3 says laws and regulations designed and intended to apply to Medicare supplement policies:

options.A: Also control every long-term care policy, with no exception
options.B: Shall not be applied to long-term care insurance
options.C: Replace Chapter 42 entirely
options.D: Apply only if the long-term care policy is not called long-term care

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 33-42-3 says the chapter's requirements apply to long-term care insurance policies issued, delivered, or issued for delivery in this state. It says the chapter is not intended to supersede other applicable provisions of Title 33 insofar as they do not conflict, except that laws and regulations designed and intended to apply to Medicare supplement insurance policies shall not be applied to long-term care insurance. A policy which is not advertised, marketed, or offered as long-term care insurance need not meet the requirements of the chapter.

topic: Georgia rules for accident and sickness only
question: A health policy is not advertised, marketed, or offered as long-term care insurance. O.C.G.A. § 33-42-3 says:

options.A: It must still meet every requirement of the Long-term Care Insurance Act
options.B: It need not meet the requirements of Chapter 42
options.C: It is automatically a Medicare supplement policy
options.D: It is illegal to sell in Georgia

explanation: The last sentence of O.C.G.A. § 33-42-3 states that a policy which is not advertised, marketed, or offered as long-term care insurance need not meet the requirements of that chapter. That sentence does not reclassify the policy as a Medicare supplement policy and does not say the policy is illegal. Medicare supplement status depends on Chapter 43, including the definition in § 33-43-1(6).
